shots.visual: THIS SHOT: accomplice two, fire: a gaming card held up to the lamp glows like a small furnace, weeks shrink to a day, and a plain stack trains in one pulse with no warm-up. CAMERA: a desk insert (the hands holding the graphics card up to the lamp), then the plate beside it. Occluder wipe carrying the lamp change (dawnGold to candleAmber, STUDY LOCK): the night side of the turning paper globe sweeps across frame and reveals the study desk in the banker's lamp's amber pool. The detective's hands hold a long double-slot consumer graphics card (generic `gpuCard`, no marks, two fans) up to the lamp like a jeweller with a stone. Date stamp bottom left. On 'fire' the fans spin up and the card's vents breathe an orange glow: the card becomes a small paper furnace, embers drifting up on L5 through haze on L3 (the image the clue card will keep). The era colour lives only in this practical: the furnace glow, never the room's lamp. On 'seventy' a teaching inset on a parchment plate beside it: two paper clocks, a CPU's hands crawling across several weeks while the card's clock sweeps once to about a day (Raina, Madhavan and Ng, 2009), with the speed-up label. On 'record' the clocks slide off the plate and the kit `lanternNetwork` stack from ch07-s02 takes their place, ONE image: a handwritten digit wobbling as if reflected in water (elastic deformation, IDSIA's training trick) feeds the stack's bottom row as its input, and the rows light ALL AT ONCE from random weights, no row-by-row warm-up; the record label pins beneath. On 'warm-up' the empty warm-up row-by-row cue (a faint ghost of the bottom-to-top sweep from ch07-s02) flickers and is struck through by the single all-at-once pulse. Camera: a lateral truck across the held card (x ±80) with a 3% push-in; the embers on L5 and the haze on L3 sell the depth.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the warm-up candle gutters at an uncertain ring; its tag goes onto the coat hook, the X-ray column's fourth band lights, and the two accomplices' clue cards are pinned. CAMERA: SHELF (low macro; the warm-up candle gutters), then the board's edge (the coat hook), then X-RAY (square-on, band 4), then BOARD (the C3-a and C3-b pins as inserts). Crossfade within the study (candleAmber throughout, STUDY LOCK): the graphics card's furnace glow dissolves into a candle flame, and the camera settles on the long paper-cut candle shelf beneath the case board, where the 2006 candle is seen for the first time in its place, to the right of the 1990s candle (ch07-s02 no longer cuts away to it). CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. The 2006 candle (DEEP NETS MUST BE WARMED UP LAYER BY LAYER) has a ghost sleeve about five rings long; on 'guttered' its flame shrinks, a thread of smoke rises and curls, and the TOP of the ghost sleeve is left with a soft, FRAYED edge rather than a clean cut (the end date is uncertain), with a small hanging tag: 'c. 2006 – c. 2010–12'. Just after the line, wordless (ch11-s01 pays this image off), the hands ink the word PRE-TRAINING on the blank tag tied to the stub since ch07-s02 and lift it off. Instead of filing it, they tie it (the same hand action as a pin) to the sleeve of a dusty paper-cut frock coat hanging on a brass hook beside the board's right edge, outside the grid; the tag sways against the coat. Frame this exactly as ch11-s01 will open on it: coat and hook in the right third, the board's edge at left (the planted rhyme; it returns in ch11). Then, music only, overlapping the last of the tie (ORDER, timed by the beats: ink the tag; tie it to the coat; the X-ray fades up while the tag still sways, and holds; only as it fades are the clue cards pinned and the threads lit, before the shot ends): the X-ray chat box from the prologue fades up at frame right and holds, a little more translucent than last time, glowing serverCyan as a practical in the amber room; of its seven faint strata (laid out in ch02-s08), exactly one new band lights, slowly and unmistakably, the fourth from the bottom: racks of graphics cards and a sea of text, above the already-lit bands of threshold units, weights, and hidden layers with the backward arrow. Last image: the hands pin this chapter's two clue cards at the head of column C3: in C3-a a small grid of a thousand tiny tiles (data, ImageNet), and in C3-b, just beneath it, a paper-cut of two small furnaces (fire). BOARD MAP (canonical, from the staging appendix; repeated word for word): the Case Board is a fixed grid of slots laid out as network columns by era, left to right: C1 (1943–1969) the far-left input column, C2 (1969–1997), C3 (2006–2017), C4 (2018–2023), and the output, the glowing chat box, at the far right; the case card WHO TAUGHT IT? hangs in slot K at the board's centre; the suspect cards S1 RULES, S2 KNOWLEDGE and S3 LEARNING hang in the left margin, top to bottom; the founding row F1–F2 runs beneath columns C3 and C4; the question-card thread runs along the board's top edge (slots Q1 to Q4, left to right), a low-chroma oxblood string (emberRed rim mixed about 60% into candleAmber) that glints only where the lamp's pool falls; the Wall of Forecasts hangs to the board's right, its slots W1 to W8 left to right (W1 Turing, W2 chess, W3 Rosenblatt 1961, W4 Florence 2012, W5 Coulom, W6 the 30-to-50-years slip in shadow, W7 Hinton 2017, W8 an empty pin until ch15). A thread of light runs from the two clue cards to the pierced-stencil card (1989) and the backward-bead card (1986) in their slots.

chapters.title: DEEP DIVE — The Night in Florence
chapters.blurb: 2011 to 2013. AlexNet, built part by part in Hinton's Toronto lab: a photo as a grid of lights, one stencil and its worked number (a convolution), stencils on stencils, stencils learned from noise, a weir that keeps strong signals strong, too few labels for sixty million knobs (crops, mirrors, and dropout, so no lantern can count on another), two halves that split the work their own way, and five days downhill. Then Florence, 12 October 2012, without its professor: 15.3% against 26.2%, a cliff, then the fair caveats. Two candles go out (speech had gone first; within a year every top team used such nets), one is lit and gets its name, deep learning, a desk lamp at the rim clicks on after thirty-six years, and a prophecy goes on the Wall.

shots.setting: the study's candle shelf, then a craftsman's workshop, 2010–2011, evening: tin stencils cut by hand, a judge's lectern, a leaderboard of lanterns

lines.text: Since about 1999, the belief: to see, a machine needs patterns designed by experts, by hand. Even allowed five guesses a picture, the best program missed more than one in four.
lines.direction: respectful of the craft; the belief stated as a reasonable belief, no irony yet; the date plainly
lines.spoken: Since about nineteen ninety-nine, the belief: to see, a machine needs patterns designed by experts, by hand. Even allowed five guesses a picture, the best program missed more than one in four.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the expert-features candle is set on the shelf; in a craftsman's workshop tin stencils are cut by hand, and even with five guesses a quarter of the ring of pictures goes dark. CHAPTER INDEX TAB (the film's chapter-card device for clue chapters): at the shot's first frame a manila index tab, typed in Special Elite with the chapter title 'DEEP DIVE · The Night in Florence', drops down from the frame's top edge at frame top-left like a file-divider tab, holds for 2.5 seconds over the picture, and slides back up; no new shot, no lamp change. CAMERA: SHELF (low macro; the expert-features candle set in its year's place), then the occluder wipe into the workshop. Opens in the study (candleAmber, the film's home base); the tab rides over the start of the first line. Under it, the two steady hands bring a tall candle into the lamp's pool; on 'belief' (as the narration states the belief and its date aloud) they set it on the candle shelf beneath the board, into its year's place (left of the 2006 warm-up candle; CANDLE PLACEMENT), lettered (paraphrase, small caps, Plex Mono) TO SEE, A MACHINE NEEDS FEATURES DESIGNED BY EXPERTS; its base tag reads 'lit 1999'. CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. Here eleven rings have already burned (1999 to 2010): a ghost sleeve of eleven scored rings (66 px) stands above the stub, the flame live where sleeve meets stub. On 'experts' a sheet of dark paper is drawn across frame by an unseen hand (an in-shot occluder wipe, same lamp, never a dim to black) and we are in a paper-cut workshop: a craftsman's silhouette (generic, no likeness) at a bench under a hanging lamp cuts patterns into small tin plates with snips: little gradient arrows, corner marks, edge combs (the hand-designed features of the age, stylised). Finished stencils hang on hooks along the back wall like tools. He carries a stencil to a tall judge's lectern at frame right; behind it a LEADERBOARD OF LANTERNS: paper lanterns hung on strings, each lantern's height = that year's winning error (lower is better), on a ruled scale. On 'five' a single thumbnail (a husky) is pinned on the lectern with five small paper guess-slips fanned beneath it; one slip is the right answer, so the guess counts (top-5 scoring, shown, not said). On 'best' two lanterns glow: 2010 at 28.2%, 2011 at 25.8%, barely a hand's width apart. On 'four' a little more than a quarter of a ring of thumbnails beside the board goes dark (both years missed more than one in four). Date stamp bottom left. TEXT RULE: besides stamps and name cards, at most two text items in this shot.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a Toronto bedroom at night: Sutskever talks Krizhevsky into trying, two gaming cards spin up in a desktop tower, and the lamp clicks off onto a green LED. Plain cut (same candleAmber lamp). Paper-cut bedroom at night (keep décor minimal and generic, after the CHM's photograph of the home computer; invent nothing): a desk, a desk lamp, a window onto a dark street, and a desktop tower (`desktopTower`, gpus: 2, window panel) on the floor. lines.text: A photograph is a grid of lights, each light a number. In colour, three numbers: red, green, blue. One small photo: a hundred and fifty thousand numbers.
lines.direction: simple and clear; the first step of the build; 'red, green, blue' set down one at a time; 'a hundred and fifty thousand' plain, letting the size land

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: match cut: the Mark I's 20 × 20 photocell eye subdivides into a modern photograph, a grid of lights, each light a number, in three colour planes. Mood stays candleAmber from the bedroom (the desk lamp has just clicked off; the LED-to-cell dissolve carries the light, and the pixel grid's own glow is the shot's practical, so no tint jump). Teaching machine `perceptronRetina` in close-up: the Mark I's 20 × 20 photocell eye from ch03, its four hundred cells glowing on a horizontal bar, stamped BUFFALO · 1958–60 (the Mark I's contested build date, as in ch03-s04 and ch06-s01). The green LED from the last shot dissolves into one of its cells. Camera pulls back as the grid subdivides and multiplies: 400 cells become a 224 × 224 field that resolves into a small backlit photograph (a husky, one of ImageNet's thousand tiles), then, on 'colour', the photo separates like three sheets of coloured tissue into red, green and blue planes stacked in depth, each pixel a tiny lit square. On 'number' one pixel is picked out by a lens and a typed value appears beside it (e.g. 0.73). Just after the line the three planes slide back together and the equation 224 × 224 × 3 = 150,528 is set in Plex Mono, held in the music. Date stamp changes from BUFFALO · 1958–60 to TORONTO · 2012. The count (about a hundred and fifty thousand numbers) is carried on screen only. SCRIPT NOTE (review round 1): L0805 now names the colour planes and the count: the planes separate on 'colour', and 224 × 224 × 3 = 150,528 sets on 'hundred'.

shots.setting: a stitched tapestry of the digit 4, a pierced 3 × 3 tin lantern, and a wall that fills with spots of light

lines.text: Hold a pierced tin stencil over the picture, a light behind it.
lines.direction: slow, demonstrative, like holding up a real object

lines.text: Each of its nine holes weighs the light beneath it. Add them up. Below zero counts as zero.
lines.direction: three distinct steps, a beat between each

lines.text: Over an edge, the sum is nearly four: a bright spot. Now the lovely part: slide the same stencil everywhere. A convolution.
lines.direction: the payoff; 'the sum is nearly four' plainly, the number landing on the bright spot; real delight on 'Now the lovely part'; let the slide fall in rhythm with the stencil's steps; then name the idea plainly, as a gift

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a pierced 3 × 3 tin stencil over a stitched digit: nine holes weigh the light, the sum is inked, below zero goes dark, and the same stencil slides everywhere to fill a wall of bright spots. WORD RULE: the narration calls this object a tin stencil; 'lantern' is reserved film-wide for units (the lantern network), so no label or caption here calls the stencil a lantern (the kit name `stencilLantern` stays internal). Teaching machine `stencilLantern` (kernel 'vertical', the real Sobel-style weights −1 0 1 / −2 0 2 / −1 0 1), staged as a paper theatre: the stitched 14 × 14 tapestry of a handwritten '4' at left, the pierced tin stencil hanging over it, the plaster wall at right where its beam falls, ruled into the 12 × 12 feature map. Pierced holes are positive weights (sized by the weight), dark shutters with a cool rim are negative. On 'pierced' showKernel rises: the nine weights are inked beside the nine holes on the stencil itself (part of the machine, not a caption). On 'weighs' the camera pushes into the stencil; the nine weights glow one by one over the nine threads beneath. On 'Add' a parchment plate inks in the nine products, one per hole, middle column included (its weights are zero, so those three terms are visibly 0). On 'zero' a shuttered position over the stroke's right edge shows its sum, −4, rectified to 0: the wall cell stays dark. On 'edge' the stencil glides to the stroke's LEFT edge (row 10, column 7, step 127); the parchment plate shows the worked cell with all nine real values in row order (window rows 0.12 0.24 1 / 0 0.12 1 / 0 0.12 1, verified against DIGIT4 and convolve() in stencilLantern.ts): max(0, (−1)(0.12) + (0)(0.24) + (1)(1) + (−2)(0) + (0)(0.12) + (2)(1) + (−1)(0) + (0)(0.12) + (1)(1)) = 3.88; the beam flares and the brightest spot on the wall lights. On 'Slide' the stencil returns to step 0 and steps in raster order, on twos, accelerating, each wall cell lighting with its real rectified dot product until the full feature map glows: a bright vertical bar wherever a stroke's left edge is. On 'convolution' the camera eases back: the one stencil's shadow is seen repeated, faintly, at every position across the wall (the same nine weights everywhere). Hold on the finished wall in the music. An ILLUSTRATIVE tag sits small at frame bottom from 'pierced' on: this hand-set 3 × 3 stencil on a 14 × 14 digit is a teaching toy; AlexNet's real first-layer stencils are 96 learned 11 × 11 colour stencils (ch08-s05/s06). The general formula spot = max(0, Σ wᵢ · xᵢ) moves to the end-credits sources card; the narration says it in words. TEXT RULE: besides stamps and name cards, at most two text items in this shot. The kernel's numbers live on the stencil; the −4 → 0 shows only as the wall cell's own value.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a cathedral of stencils rises from the photograph's rose window, five courses of detectors built from detectors, then two great halls and a last hall of a thousand lanterns. Teaching machine `alexnetCathedral` (labels on). The husky photograph from s03 becomes the ROSE WINDOW at the base of a two-tower cathedral façade against a dawnGold sky. On 'ninety-six' the first course of stone rises: the conv1 blocks with face width 55 (true shape), and on the rose window's tracery 96 tiny 11 × 11 tiles flicker in (the first-layer stencils). On 'four' the second course rises at face width 27, then three courses at 13, 13, 13 (reveal driven block by block). Between courses, as each course face narrows (55 to 27, 27 to 13), a tiny wordless 3 × 3 window passes over the lower course's bright spots and keeps only the brightest cell of each window (overlapping max-pooling, 3 × 3, stride 2: a diagram mark, no caption), so the eye sees why the picture shrinks, each block's windows lighting as the flow climbs; on 'stencilling' the bright spots of one course are seen feeding up as the picture the next course's stencils slide over (detectors built from detectors). The layer vignettes appear ONE AT A TIME, in the rose-window position itself (never as simultaneous insets): as each course lights, the rose window briefly shows what such a layer responds to, then returns to the photograph: on 'edges' oriented strokes; on 'textures' woven textures; on 'parts' a fur patch and an eye; on 'things' a whole dog's head. On 'halls' TWO great halls rise above the five courses (fc6 and fc7, 4,096 lanterns each; in each, threads fan from every lantern to every lantern below, 'every lantern sees everything'), and on 'last' a third, last hall rises above them that IS a band of a thousand small lanterns, one per category, each with a tiny category tag (fc8, the output; nothing stacks above it; WORD RULE: 'door' is reserved for the chat box in ch12, so this band is never drawn as doors), as the camera pulls back to see the whole cathedral. (Five stencil courses plus three fully connected stages, two great halls and the hall of a thousand lanterns: the paper's five convolutional and three fully connected layers. 'The great halls' in ch08-s08b means exactly the two big halls, fc6 and fc7.) Breaths are opened in the narration after 'edges', 'textures' and 'parts' so each vignette reads (about a second each), not a flicker. Then hold in the music (about 2.5 s) while flow light climbs from window to crown, course by course: as the light reaches each course the rose window replays that course's vignette, one per course (strokes, textures, fur and eye, the dog's head), and settles back to the photograph as the crown lights. No new stair geometry anywhere. TEXT RULE: besides stamps and name cards, at most two text items in this shot. The paper's 'depth really is important' line moves to the end-credits sources card. shots.visual: THIS SHOT: 96 tiles of television snow are nudged, pass after pass, into the learned mosaic by the 1986 bead. CAMERA: the cathedral's rose window (teaching machine) only; no board insert. Close on the rose window's 96 tiles: they are pure static, grey random speckle. On 'messenger' the dark bead in a ring of light from ch05 (the `lanternNetwork` backward pulse, same design) appears at the cathedral's crown and runs DOWN the cathedral's existing paths only (the column shafts and the bridges between the towers already in `alexnetCathedral`; no new stair geometry), past every course, to the rose window; as it passes each block it tugs its stencils a hair. On 'nudge' the cycle repeats faster and faster (picture after picture: tiny thumbnails flick through the rose window); with each pass the static tiles sharpen until they resolve into the real first-layer mosaic: striped grey edges at every angle and soft colour blobs. The long paper-cut candle shelf beneath the case board. CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. Three candles matter here. The expert-features candle (TO SEE, A MACHINE NEEDS FEATURES DESIGNED BY EXPERTS, tag 'lit 1999'): on 'thirteen' it gutters and goes out with thirteen rings burned (1999 to 2012), a dark ghost sleeve of thirteen scored rings (78 px) above its stub, a thread of smoke rising; its tag is re-inked '1999 – 2012 · 13'. chapters.title: The Gold Rush
chapters.blurb: 2012–2017. The 2012 candle becomes a creed: deep learning works on everything. By one reporter's account, a man who will not sit auctions a company of three to Google; DeepMind's Go machine, which learned from people, then from itself, arrives about eight years early, and Lee Sedol answers it once; months before Seoul, OpenAI is founded on hope and fear. At the rim, doubters, and the candle burns on; then a slip goes up on the Wall, and nobody says a word.

shots.setting: Lake Tahoe, Nevada, December 2012, late night: a hotel room (Room 731), a laptop propped on an upturned wastebasket
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a hotel room at Lake Tahoe: a new candle's pool spreads across the floor as sealed bids slide along a thread and the tall man stops the auction. CHAPTER INDEX TAB (the film's chapter-card device for clue chapters): at the shot's first frame a manila index tab, typed in Special Elite with the chapter title 'The Gold Rush', drops down from the frame's TOP edge at top-left, like a file-divider tab (the manila tab's own corner, clear of the bottom-left date and place stamps), holds for 2.5 seconds over the picture, and slides back up; no new shot, no lamp change. CAMERA: the hotel room (era location; no study visit), the creed candle on its stage in the out-of-focus foreground. Hard match cut (same serverCyan mood as chapter 8's last shot, so no lamp change): on the blink of chapter 8's green status LED, its glow becomes the cool screen of a laptop in a dark hotel room. Wide, static at first. Mid-plane: a tall man in silhouette (Hinton, 2000s–2020s puppet, blazer, swept-back hair) STANDS, straight-backed, at a laptop balanced on an upturned wastebasket, the only way he can type standing. Behind him a window of black pines and a band of snow-light; a hotel bed he never sits on, cut as one flat dark shape. On 'account' a small label, 'as reported by Cade Metz', sets in at lower left and stays for the whole shot: everything in this room is one reporter's account. Foreground, out of focus: the new candle from chapter 8, LEARNED FEATURES, GIVEN DATA AND ARITHMETIC, now huge on a paper stage (lit in 2012, its ghost sleeve not yet one ring tall), and its pool of light falls exactly where he stands. CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. THE CREED (L0901): the shot opens racked to the foreground candle; on 'candle' its flame steadies and brightens; on 'everything' its pool of light spreads outward across the whole floor of the room, to the walls and under the bed, as if no corner were out of its reach (deep learning, believed to work everywhere; L0901 'A new candle, then a creed' names it aloud for the first time; no text, the candle keeps burning). Then the focus racks to the standing man for L0902. This is the payoff of the Edge of the Light: the man we met at the rim, seated at desks, now stands in the centre of the light. Slow push-in (about 6% over the shot). On 'tall' the pool brightens around his feet. On 'three-person' a small tilt down shows the laptop on the upturned wastebasket (the narration names neither; the picture carries both). On 'auctioned', four sealed paper envelopes slide in along a thread from the dark at frame right, each a bid; their wax seals glow and swell with each round. Just after 'company' one envelope (the earliest bidder) drops off the thread; a second drops soon after; the bids climb on a typewritten tally that ticks up in the screen's glow. On 'forty-four' his hand lifts off the keys, palm down, and the tally freezes at 44,000,000. On 'Google', the line's last word (beat choseGoogle), his hand draws one of the two remaining envelopes off the thread and lays it face UP beside the laptop, its typed address a single large word, GOOGLE, caught in the screen's glow (prop lettering on the envelope, not a label); the last envelope drifts back into the dark (the $44M lives on the frozen tally, a prop; TEXT RULE: 'as reported by Cade Metz' is the shot's only label besides the place stamp and the chapter index tab; the deal's announcement, March 2013, is in the published sources list). Ear and eye now both know his new employer, which chapter 13's 'He left Google' depends on. Hold on the still figure in the candle's pool. No logos anywhere; the bidders are blank envelopes, and Google appears only as the typed word on the chosen envelope.

shots.setting: the detective's study, night: the far end of the Wall of Forecasts, September 2017
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: at the Wall's far rim two exhibits lift into the light: a panda card flipped to gibbon by invisible changes, and two rows of faces ticked unequally by commercial software. CAMERA: WALL (a slow lateral truck with the hands, W1 to W7, then it stops), the nets' candle on the shelf at the bottom edge of frame at the lamp end. Plain cut (same candleAmber, same room; STUDY LOCK, so no lamp change) from the case board along the study to the Wall of Forecasts under the green-shaded desk lamp. WALL OF FORECASTS SLOT ORDER (BOARD MAP, canonical, word for word): its slots W1 to W8 left to right (W1 Turing, W2 chess, W3 Rosenblatt 1961, W4 Florence 2012, W5 Coulom, W6 the 30-to-50-years slip in shadow, W7 Hinton 2017, W8 an empty pin until ch15). (W2 has been an empty pin since chapter 6.) THE DOUBTERS (L0910): the lamp's pool lies wide over the Wall, and at its RIM (in this film the rim is reserved for doubters) two paper exhibits stand half in shadow on the side table, objects only, no figures. On 'doubters' the lamp's edge brightens a little to find them. On 'Changes' the first exhibit lifts into the light: a small stencil-card picture of a panda, its typed caption a prop on the card ('panda 57.7%'); a fine dust of specks drifts over it, so faint the eye barely finds it, and on 'fool' the caption flips to 'gibbon 99.3%' while the picture itself does not visibly change (small typed credit on the card: Goodfellow, Shlens & Szegedy, 2014). On 'commercial' the second exhibit lifts: a parchment plate with two rows of cut-paper face silhouettes, one row darker paper, one lighter; on 'darker-skinned' a stamp of oxblood ticks falls across the darker row, and only a single tick across the lighter row on 'lighter-skinned'; the Gender Shades label sets in beneath the plate (it states what was measured: gender misread, not faces in general) and stays pinned at frame edge until the slip is pinned in W7 (beat slipPinned). Neutral, factual staging: the exhibits are evidence, not villains. THE CANDLE BURNED ON (the creed lit aloud in ch09-s01 gets its fate stated): on 'candle', at the bottom of the frame on the shelf beneath the Wall, at the lamp end where the truck will start, the lamp catches the nets' own candle, LEARNED FEATURES, GIVEN DATA AND ARITHMETIC, tag 2012: a live flame, its ghost sleeve five rings tall and still growing (the belief was ratified, not refuted; its sleeve keeps growing into chapter 10). CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. Then the slip: at the end of the line the lamp's pool begins to narrow away from the rim, and the hands lift a new paper slip into the light (no caption; its typed lettering stays a prop) and carry it along the Wall, left to right, the camera trucking with them from W1 to W7 (the WALL camera's slow lateral truck), past every other forecast: Turing's curling slip (slot 1), the chess slip's empty pin (slot 2), Rosenblatt's slip (slot 3), the 2012 GPU slip (slot 4), Coulom's glinting pin (slot 5), and then slot 6, the 30-to-50-years slip, which stays in deep shadow: only its lower corner catches the lamp, half-lit, its words unreadable (a plant; it is read in chapter 13). The hands pin the new slip in W7, just beyond it (W8, the far end, stays an empty pin until ch15): dissent from the movement's own leader. The truck stops at W7 and holds still. The hands withdraw; the lamp's pool narrows and rests on this slip alone, and the two exhibits at the rim fall back into shadow. The slip is recognisable at a glance and must stay so for its return in chapter 15: it is the only slip on the Wall whose due-date box is blank, a small empty typed box on its tail, with a plain brass pin. Its large first clause catches the lamp only once it is pinned, in a hold that is mostly music only (the slip's tail carries a small typed prop credit, 'as quoted by G. Marcus, 2018', not a label; only its first clause is typed large, the rest of the sentence small and illegible, saved for ch15-s09). Nobody speaks after the doubters' line: the narrator deliberately says nothing about the slip. A single draught moves the slip's corner once, late in the hold. This is the plant for the film's last spoken quotation (chapter 15). TEXT RULE: besides stamps and name cards, at most one text item in this shot (the Gender Shades label); the panda captions are typed on the prop. ROUND 5 (runtime): the carried slip is NOT captioned here; its typed lettering stays small and only half-caught by the lamp, a plant like the W6 slip in shadow. It is read aloud and shown in full, with its attribution, in ch15-s09.

lines.text: At the rim, doubters. Changes too small to see could fool these nets. Joy Buolamwini and Timnit Gebru found commercial face software misread the gender of darker-skinned women far more often than of lighter-skinned men. The candle burned on, and still does, argued over.
lines.direction: fair and steady, the voice of a careful witness; no alarm, no scolding; 'too small to see' with quiet wonder; the two names unhurried and clear; the face finding given its full, plain weight; 'The candle burned on, and still does, argued over.' level and quiet, neither triumph nor warning; then silence for the slip

Under L0910 a thin low drone only, with one dry muted tick on 'fool' and soft ticks under the falling stamp; on 'candle burned on' the candle motif's rising fourth, very soft, unresolved (the creed still lit); nothing ominous, nothing resolving. chapters.title: DEEP DIVE — Everything Looks at Everything
chapters.blurb: 2014–2018. The Transformer, built one part at a time. For twenty years language had to be read in order; then attention, and a lunch-table idea that colleagues doubted. Fire the slow reader, keep the attention: three cards per word, one jug of light, a division by eight, eight heads, a clock face for position, talk then think six times. The title, why it won and what it costs, a twenty-year candle put out, and the writing half of the machine, with its curtain over the words to come.

shots.setting: a long, high hall of hanging paper word-slips at dusk, out of time (the inside of a recurrent network); the candle shelf at its foot
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a long hall of hanging word-slips where a scribe carries one lamp from slip to slip in order, and the light he carries fades to a glow-worm at the far end. CHAPTER INDEX TAB (the film's chapter-card device for clue chapters): at the shot's first frame a manila index tab, typed in Special Elite with the chapter title 'DEEP DIVE · Everything Looks at Everything', drops down from the frame's top edge at top-left, like a file-divider tab on a manila folder, holds for 2.5 seconds over the picture, and slides back up; no new shot, no lamp change. CAMERA: the long hall (era location), with one SHELF ledge slid into its foreground (low macro on the read-in-order candle). From black, a single lamp, under the tab. Silently, in the lead-in (no line names it), a ghost of chapter 8's pierced stencil hangs in the haze above the hall and thins away into it (convolution is not in the Transformer; only its lesson, learn the features, carries on), before the scribe sets off. We are at one end of a very long hall: a line of paper word-slips hangs from a beam, receding into haze, dozens of them. A small cut-paper scribe (no real person) walks the line with one lamp, stopping at every slip in turn: he reads it, then passes the lamp's flame forward to a wick on the next slip, step by step, on twos. The camera tracks with him slowly, then pulls back to show how long the line is. This is chapter 6's whisper made visible: the light he carries dims a little at each hand-off, so by the far end it is a glow-worm (the vanishing signal; at about slip 50 it is nearly gone). On 'candle' a short ledge of the candle shelf slides into the hall's foreground and its candle is picked out, standing in its year's place on the shelf (CANDLE PLACEMENT: by the year on the base tag, so left of the 1999 and 2006 candles) (STUDY LOCK: the candle's own flame throws a small candleAmber pool, a practical inside the duskRose hall; the study shelf proper is seen in candleAmber in ch10-s13b): LANGUAGE MUST BE READ IN ORDER (lettered on the candle itself in small caps; base tag 1997). CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. Here the candle is still lit: a ghost sleeve about seventeen rings tall (102 px) stands above the stub, the flame where sleeve meets stub; it will go out at twenty rings in ch10-s13b. At its foot, small, the chapter 6 'protected pipe' (the long-memory unit) glows on 'pipe', the callback the line makes: the date the candle was lit, and the reason the belief held so long. In the short music-only hold after L1002 the glow-worm light crawls on down the long dim line (Polosukhin's 'a thousand cycles' quote moves to the end-credits sources card).

shots.setting: a parchment plate in a translator's study, 2014: English word-slips across the top, French down the side
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a whole sentence folded into one envelope jams in a funnel; then the plate opens into a grid where each French word looks back at every English word. Cut (same mood, same sequence) to a parchment plate. First, the old way, as the narration names it. A whole English sentence is folded, slip by slip, into one small sealed envelope (the single list of numbers), and the envelope is squeezed through a narrow paper funnel before a French sentence is written out on the far side. As the sentence is squeezed into the funnel the Bahdanau quote card sets in beside it and stays up through the line, read under the narration (the narration names the bottleneck as the envelope jams; the card shows whose word it was). Then the plate opens into a grid: English slips along the top ('the agreement on the European Economic Area'), French slips down the side ('l'accord sur la zone économique européenne'), the words lettered on the slips themselves (no overlay). As each French word is written, a highlighter of light sweeps across the English row and squares light by how much the translator looks back at each word. The lit squares march along the diagonal and then BEND where French reverses the order (European Economic Area → zone économique européenne), forming the classic alignment heat-map. Every visual square is bound to an attention weight; the map is redrawn from the paper's figure, not copied.

lines.text: In 2014, translating machines squeezed a whole sentence into one list of numbers: a bottleneck. So they learned to look back at every word: attention.
lines.spoken: In twenty fourteen, translating machines squeezed a whole sentence into one list of numbers: a bottleneck. So they learned to look back at every word: attention.
lines.direction: a turn, lighter; 'attention' set down gently like a key on a table

shots.setting: Google, 2016: a Google cafe table at lunch; a warmer dinner-table pool at the rim
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: lunch at Google, 2016: the ghost scribe is lifted away from the table as Uszkoreit suggests keeping only the attention, and a colleague at the rim shrugs. Cut to a sunny-dusk cafe: a long table, trays, two figures in silhouette across from each other. A tall man (Uszkoreit) sketches with a fork in the air; across the table, Polosukhin. On 'only' a ghost of the scribe from shot 1 appears above the table and is lifted away by a paper hand: keep the attention, drop the slow reader. Then the Edge of the Light: a small new lamp stands on the table and its pool spreads. In the breath before L1007 a colleague (Kelcey) steps into the rim, in shadow and facing out; on 'doubted' he gives a brief shrug. As he steps in, Kelcey's quote card rises beside him and stays up through the line and the music-only hold after L1007, so it can be read; in the hold nothing else moves but the haze and the lamp. Two images that teach one thing: a new light, and doubt at its rim.

shots.setting: the hall of word-slips from shot 1, 2017: the scribe is gone
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the scribe sets down his lamp and leaves; every slip lights at once with threads between every pair, and the banner inks The Transformer. KIT DEPENDENCY (blocking for film-shots, see staging.kitWork): threadsOfLight must accept a {tokens, weights[h][i][j]} override (it is hard-wired to the kit's sample sentence). Crossfade back to the long hall with a tint crossfade (crossfadeMood duskRose to serverCyan, no dip to black; the line waits until the cyan is fully up). On 'Drop' the scribe sets his lamp down and simply walks out of frame. On 'attention' the slips hang dark for a held beat, the abandoned lamp's small pool the only light. Then, on 'once', every slip lights at the same instant and threads of light shoot between every pair of slips at once (threadsOfLight, all queries, low opacity), so the hall fills with a fine web of light in a single step instead of a slow procession. The camera, which tracked slowly in shot 1, now holds still: nothing needs to travel. On 'Transformer' its name, THE TRANSFORMER, inks itself onto a parchment banner (prop lettering) hung from the beam (the abstract's phrase moves to the end-credits sources card); on 'title' (L1024) the paper's title inks itself beneath it on the same banner, ATTENTION IS ALL YOU NEED, prop lettering in the banner's own hand; and with it, a third, smaller line in the same hand lists all eight authors in the paper's own order (its footnote says the order is random, and all contributed equally): Vaswani · Shazeer · Parmar · Uszkoreit · Jones · Gomez · Kaiser · Polosukhin (the 2017 date stamp sits beside it), so no one leaves thinking it was a two-person lunch idea (the deadline night, the title's coining and the random author order are in the published sources list), and the web glows through a short hold.

lines.text: Drop the word-by-word reader, keep the attention: every word looks at every other, all at once. The Transformer.

shots.setting: close on three word-slips in the hall, 2017
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: one word-slip turns into numbers and grows three cards, a lantern (question), a mirror (label) and a sealed note (message), each on a knob the messenger tunes. Close on one hanging word-slip. On 'numbers' the slip's lettering briefly dissolves into a short column of small inked numerals (a word is a list of numbers to the machine), then settles back. As each card is named, the slip grows it: on 'question' a small paper lantern with a beam (the query: it shines outward, looking for something); on 'label' a small hand mirror with a tag (the key: what this word offers to be found by); on 'message' a sealed paper note (the value: what it hands over if chosen). On 'tuned' three small brass knobs (the film's 1958 knob, the adjustable weight) appear between the slip and its three objects, one knob per card, each turned to its own setting; just after the line, wordless, the dark messenger bead from chapter 5, in its ring of light, runs once along the three knobs and each turns a hair: the cards are made from the word by learned weights, tuned by back-propagation. Then pull back: every slip in the row now carries all three, lantern, mirror and note, the same three objects in every word, and one caption builds up beneath them as each card is named. The objects are drawn the same everywhere from here on, so a viewer can follow them through the next three shots.

lines.text: Each word arrives as a learned list of numbers and grows three cards: a question, what am I looking for? A label, what have I got? A message, what I pass on. All tuned by our messenger.
lines.direction: the teacher's favourite bit; the first sentence plain and grounding, then three clear steps, warm on 'what I pass on'; the last sentence lighter: these cards are learned, not written

shots.setting: a parchment plate hung from the beam in the hall: four word-slips and four lantern-glass cups
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the worked example: bank shines its question on four mirrors, scores 2, 0, 4, 2 are halved, one jug of light pours into four cups, and bank tints to the water's edge. KIT DEPENDENCY (blocking for film-shots, see staging.kitWork): threadsOfLight and attentionMath need {tokens: crossed · the · river · bank, weights, cups: 4, etched shares} overrides; the kit's toy heads are wired to a different sentence. Cut (same mood, same sequence) to a parchment plate hung from the beam in the hall, a small ILLUSTRATIVE tag in its corner. Four word-slips in a row: crossed · the · river · bank. 'bank' raises its small lantern (its question) and the beam touches each slip's mirror (label) in turn. On 'multiply' the gesture of the chapter 8 stencil returns: bank's four question numbers line up against the label's four, each pair multiplies (small ink products), and on 'add' they sum into one score (the dot product, the same multiply-and-add as the stencil). As each match is scored, the score inks beside its slip: 2, 0, 4, 2. On 'halve' a pen strikes through each score and writes the halves beneath: 1, 0, 2, 1. Then a jug of light tips over the row and pours into four lantern-glass cups beneath the slips; the levels are the real softmax of those halved scores, so the cups fill to 20, 7, 53 and 20 in a hundred, each share etched on its own cup's glass (0.20 · 0.07 · 0.53 · 0.20), the river cup clearly fullest. On 'messages' each word's sealed note (its message) is poured out of its cup into 'bank' in those same proportions, river's note by far the largest stream; on 'water's' bank's slip tints from gold to water-blue, and a small meter drawn on the plate settles at water 0.53 · action 0.20 · money 0.20. The numbers are computed (scaled dot product over toy four-number cards), not hand-drawn; the bible's worked example.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: two plates side by side: unscaled scores slam all the light into one cup and learning freezes; divided by eight, the jug pours softly. KIT DEPENDENCY (blocking for film-shots, see staging.kitWork): attentionMath needs {cups: 3, scores, etched shares} overrides for the two jug panels. The plate widens into two panels with the same jug and three cups. LEFT, unscaled, cards of sixty-four numbers: the scores ink large on the panel, 8 · 0 · −8. shots.setting: the hall of word-slips, 2017: the announcement's example sentence hung across the beam
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the full-size echo of the toy on the hall's banner sentence: bank's threads reach every slip, then the light splits into coloured heads, each with its own pattern. KIT DEPENDENCY (blocking for film-shots, see staging.kitWork): threadsOfLight needs {tokens: the nine-word sentence, weights[h][i][j] hand-set, cups: 9} overrides. Cut back to the wide hall (same mood). The banner of slips now reads the example sentence from Google's 2017 announcement of the Transformer, lettered on the slips: I · arrived · at · the · bank · after · crossing · the · river. A small ILLUSTRATIVE tag hangs at the banner's end. At the shot's first beat the banner settles (the line no longer speaks the look; the picture carries it); on 'real' the slip 'bank' lifts its lantern and threads of light draw out from 'bank' to every other slip (threadsOfLight, query = 'bank', with HAND-SET weights for this sentence; the kit's attentionMath toy heads are built for a different sentence and are NOT used here), and the jug pours into cups beneath the slips; on 'Transformer' the cup under 'river' fills highest, far above the rest. HAND-SET WEIGHTS for 'bank' (one row, sums to 1): I 0.03 · arrived 0.06 · at 0.04 · the 0.04 · bank 0.08 · after 0.03 · crossing 0.10 · the 0.04 · river 0.58. These show what the announcement says a trained model can learn (it 'can learn to immediately attend to the word river'); they are not a trained model's output, and the tag says so. Then, on 'Eight', the camera pulls back and the single colour of light splits: threads in four distinct low-chroma hues fan out from 'bank' at once, each a different head with a different question, drawn from a small HAND-BUILT HEAD TABLE (also ILLUSTRATIVE, four of the eight shown; each row sums to 1 over the nine slips, the named slips taking the share given and the rest spread evenly): head 1 'what am I?' → river 0.58 (the row above); head 2 'what came just before?' → the (4th slip) 0.70; head 3 'what was done?' → arrived 0.45, crossing 0.35; head 4 'who did it?' → I 0.65. One caption: the real model had eight heads of sixty-four numbers each. Hold on the many-coloured web; then, on 'question', every other word lifts its lantern too and the hall glows: every word doing this, all at once. This shot echoes, at full size, the toy plate of ch10-s06 (same three cards, same jug, same cups).

Faintly, behind each clock, its hands' angles are traced as a thin strip of waves (sines and cosines, fast to slow): the same thing, said the way the paper says it. shots.setting: a long loom of light inside the hall, six blocks set left to right
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a long loom of six blocks: in each, threads pass between the words, then each word brightens alone, and the light front travels through all six. KIT DEPENDENCY (blocking for film-shots, see staging.kitWork): transformerLoom needs {causal:false} and horizontal layout. Cut (same mood, same sequence): each word-slip now spools out a ribbon of light (its residual stream) running left to right through a great loom laid out horizontally, transformerLoom with causal: false (this is the 2017 reading half, the encoder, so its threads reach both ways, forward and back). The loom has six blocks in a row. In each block an attention loom passes threads BETWEEN the ribbons (the words talking; thread alpha = the kit's recorded forward pass), then each ribbon passes through its own small paper lantern (the feed-forward step, thinking alone; glow = its activation), and both write back into the ribbon. The camera trucks slowly left to right along the loom as the light front travels (flow), the focus stepping through blocks 0 to 5, six in all, while the original ribbon runs straight through every block like a highway lane (visual only: no line names it). In the music-only hold after L1021 the lane is picked out in light. The weights are illustrative: the film's standard small ILLUSTRATIVE tag sits lower-right (as in ch10-s06 and ch08-s09); no other caption (review round 4 removed the centred honesty caption).

shots.setting: a rack of eight chips on a parchment plate; a sundial; the hall of slips again
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: why it won: the web collapses into one grid lit on eight graphics chips at once; the catch: doubling the sentence thickens the threads into a wall. Paper wipe: the loom's last frame (ch10-s10) slides off and becomes the parchment plate (same mood, no tint change). The plate: one machine drawn as a single rack with eight slabs. On 'multiplication' the whole web of threads from the hall collapses into a single great grid (a matrix) and all eight slabs light at once, in parallel: no queue, no scribe. On 'chips' the slabs read as what they are, eight graphics chips in one rack, each glowing with its share of the grid (the one sum such chips do best; Aidan Gomez's line on this is in the end-credits sources). Then, wordless in the pause after L1025 (L1024 has already said it won in half a day; the picture shows how), ONE card: a paper sundial's shadow sweeps half a day while the card inks '12 hours' and, about 0.4 s later, 'one machine, 8 GPUs', held alone until 'wall'. The card carries that one fact and nothing else: no compute comparison, ratio or score of any kind (review rounds 3 and 4). Then THE CATCH: back in the hall, the sentence grows, slip by slip, from ten words to twenty; the web of threads between every pair thickens disproportionately until it becomes a near-solid wall of light, and a counter drawn on the beam shows the pairs going 100 → 400 as the length doubles.

lines.text: Why did it win? No waiting in line: all at once is one huge multiplication, just what graphics chips do best.
lines.direction: brisk, practical; a quick question, then one rolling answer landing on 'graphics chips'; leave the sundial, the compute piles and the ledger to the picture in the pause

lines.text: The catch: twice the words, four times the looking.
lines.direction: wry, the honest small print; a beat after 'catch'

shots.setting: the candle shelf below the case board, in the study (candleAmber); a dawn sky in the study window
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the read-in-order candle gutters at twenty rings while a translation lamp and a search box light; an honest card writes and crosses out three overclaims. CAMERA: the reverse flame push out to SHELF (low macro; the read-in-order candle goes out). Reverse flame push to the study shelf: the brightest knot of the wall of light from ch10-s12 becomes the flame of the read-in-order candle, and the camera pulls back out of that flame onto the shelf (never through black) while the light tint-crossfades (crossfadeMood serverCyan to candleAmber, no dip); the line waits until the amber is up. STUDY LOCK: the study is always candleAmber; the era enters only through practicals, here a dawnGold sky in the study window behind the shelf, the new day after the old belief. CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. Here LANGUAGE MUST BE READ IN ORDER (base tag 1997) has burned exactly twenty rings: a ghost sleeve twenty rings tall (120 px) stands above its stub. On 'decades' its flame gutters and goes out; the sleeve stays, dark, with a thread of smoke rising through the haze; the tag at its base now reads 1997–2017. On 'replaced' a soft cross-dissolve inside the smoke shows the new way spreading: a small lamp lit in a translation room and a search box lit in a window, each carrying a small in-world paper tag with its year, 2018 and 2019 (prop lettering, no caption) (the cross-dissolve's glow is warm dawn light through the window, never a re-tint of the study). Then, over the smoke, a parchment card writes the honest sentence one phrase at a time, wordless, starting just after L1030 ends, each phrase on its own beat: not the first attention; not only attention; built to translate. The card holds through the hold so all three can be read.

chapters.title: Read Everything
chapters.blurb: 2018–2022. Pre-training comes back in a different coat, and the attention threads light up inside the chat box. The 1985 card from the file meets a one-sentence training goal, and the typesetter's case answers the prologue's riddle of the missing rulebook. A smooth law on log paper becomes a city of a hundred and seventy-five billion weights that can learn a task from a few examples, and a new candle is lit: scale is the main lever, and the rim of its light grows crowded.

shots.setting: The detective's study, night, 2018: a brass coat-hook beside the case board; beyond the study window, a paper-cut library of raw text running to the horizon (its serverCyan glow seen through the glass)
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: wordless: X-ray band 5 (threads) lights, the old PRE-TRAINING coat is lifted off its hook and re-cut into a modern overcoat, and the camera pushes through the window into a library of raw text. CHAPTER INDEX TAB (the film's chapter-card device for clue chapters): at the shot's first frame a manila index tab, typed in Special Elite with the chapter title 'Read Everything', drops down from the frame's top edge at TOP-left like a file-divider tab, holds for 2.5 seconds over the picture, and slides back up (top-left, so it never shares the bottom-left corner with the date stamp); no new shot, no lamp change. Paper wipe (a chapter break) from ch10-s14's last frame (the writing half's ghost slot, its blank sort hanging unset) into the study, in candleAmber; the index tab rides over the lead-in. STUDY LOCK: every beat in the study, at the board, on the shelf or at the Wall is candleAmber; era colour enters only through practicals, so the library's serverCyan glow is seen only through the study window until the camera passes through it. CAMERA: X-RAY, then BOARD, then COAT, then LIBRARY. The whole shot is wordless (music only): the coat's tag and the library carry the idea; the first words of the chapter come in ch11-s02. X-RAY (wordless lead-in, moved here from ch10-s14; band 5 of the X-ray ritual): the glowing chat box from chapter 1 stands in the study, a little more translucent, its glow a serverCyan practical inside the amber room, and inside it threads of attention light up for the first time beside the threshold units, weights, hidden layers and racks already lit (only parts truly present in a modern chat model light). The camera holds on it for a full 2.4 s (as long as band 1 had), then at 2.8 s eases left to the board. BOARD (still in the lead-in): BOARD MAP (canonical, from the staging appendix; repeated word for word): the Case Board is a fixed grid of slots laid out as network columns by era, left to right: C1 (1943–1969) the far-left input column, C2 (1969–1997), C3 (2006–2017), C4 (2018–2023), and the output, the glowing chat box, at the far right; the case card WHO TAUGHT IT? hangs in slot K at the board's centre; the suspect cards S1 RULES, S2 KNOWLEDGE and S3 LEARNING hang in the left margin, top to bottom; the founding row F1–F2 runs beneath columns C3 and C4; the question-card thread runs along the board's top edge (slots Q1 to Q4, left to right), a low-chroma oxblood string (emberRed rim mixed about 60% into candleAmber) that glints only where the lamp's pool falls; the Wall of Forecasts hangs to the board's right, its slots W1 to W8 left to right (W1 Turing, W2 chess, W3 Rosenblatt 1961, W4 Florence 2012, W5 Coulom, W6 the 30-to-50-years slip in shadow, W7 Hinton 2017, W8 an empty pin until ch15). This chapter works in column C4, the last column before the output (the chat box): ch10's thread-of-light card sits at the foot of column C3, and C4's head slot C4-a waits for this chapter's type sort. The hands pin chapter 10's clue card, a thread of light between two word-slips, into slot C3-d at the foot of column C3 (beneath the furnaces in C3-b and the filter tile in C3-c), and run a faint thread of light from it to the pierced-stencil card. COAT: in the shadow beside the case board hangs the coat from chapter 7: a dusty paper-cut frock coat on a brass hook, its luggage tag lettered PRE-TRAINING in the 2000s typeface (then it meant warming a deep net up layer by layer). At 4.2 s the two steady hands lift it down and shake it out; as it swings, at 4.7 s, its silhouette re-cuts on twos into a longer, modern overcoat, and a fresh tag is stamped in IBM Plex Mono: PRE-TRAINING · READ EVERYTHING FIRST. The tag stays readable in frame until the push (4.55 s). LIBRARY: at 9.25 s the camera follows the coat past the lamp and pushes slowly through the study window, the tint crossfading (crossfadeMood, 1.2 s, no dip) from candleAmber to serverCyan as it crosses the glass, into serverCyan haze, and as it crosses, the date stamp 2018 types itself bottom-left (the index tab is long gone from the top-left): a canyon of paper-cut bookshelves to the horizon, the spines unlabelled (raw, unannotated text: first a wall of some seven thousand unpublished books, then the long pages of an encyclopedia). As the push settles (10.1 s), in music only, two small lantern-machines walk the stacks, unhurried. One reads in both directions and fills in blanked-out type slugs (BERT, Google, October 2018). The other reads strictly left to right and writes as it goes (GPT, OpenAI, June 2018). Their names appear on one shared caption only (GPT · OpenAI · BERT · Google; the 2018 stamp already stands); no other text. The camera drifts along the canyon with them and holds to the end of the shot, so the library breathes. (The 'Generating Wikipedia' blueprint thread is in ch11-s02, on the board.)

lines.text: In 2019, OpenAI’s GPT-2, a Transformer’s writing half, read some eight million web pages with one goal: “predict the next word”, or rather, the next word-piece. No labels needed: every next word is its own right answer.

shots.setting: A paper stage, 2019, night: a composing stick above a typesetter's case with six drawers; the X-ray chat box behind it
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a typesetter's case of next words: the jug of light pours into every drawer by its odds, one sort is picked and set, the stick advances, and X-ray band 6 lights. CAMERA: plate (the typesetter's case), then a pull back to X-RAY (square-on, band 6). Teaching machine: nextToken, the typesetter's case, opened up and explained for the first time; the blank sort from ch10-s14 drops into this ghost slot. In a composing stick, cast type slugs (typeSlugs) hold the words so far: 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too', a new sentence (the kit's NEXT_TOKEN_DEMO), cut short, with a faintly lit ghost slot at the end. Below, the case (cornice, broken pediment, a small lit candle on top) has six carded drawers in its lit front row, tired · wide · busy · scared · slow · dark, and behind them the case recedes into haze: thousands of tiny uncarded drawers, row behind row, toward the vanishing point (the vocabulary, tens of thousands of words). At 1.4 s, just as the narrator begins 'The jug of light now pours over every possible next word' (the line starts at 1.2 s, so the ear is told what the eye sees), chapter 10's jug of light tips and pours into the drawers, and each drawer slides out by its REAL softmax share of illustrative scores (NEXT_TOKEN_DEMO, temperature 1): tired 0.56 · wide 0.17 · busy 0.12 · scared 0.08 · slow 0.04 · dark 0.03. At 2.6 s the jug's light visibly reaches the whole receding case: every far drawer slides out a hair (the long tail), then the camera settles on the front six, whose lit lips are the bars; the six plus the hairline tail visibly sum to one. No new text: the prop lettering stays on the six. On 'Pick one', the 'tired' sort rises out of its drawer and is set in the ghost slot; the stick advances and a new ghost slot opens: ask again. Before the pick, under the end of that first sentence (3.4 to 5.6 s), a small dial labelled T is turned: at 2.5 the drawers even out (0.31 · 0.19 · 0.17 · 0.14 · 0.11 · 0.09), at 0.5 'tired' takes nearly all of it (0.85), then back to 1, so the pick on 'Pick one' follows. Then, just after the line, the camera pulls back to reveal the chat box from chapter 1 standing behind the case, and the X-ray (band 6) holds through the music-only hold to the end of the shot. X-ray beat: the box is a little more translucent, and inside it rows of next-word type sorts glow for the first time, beside the threshold units, weights, hidden layers, racks and attention threads already lit. Each drawer's lit lip carries its word and its share in small type on the prop itself (no separate caption). One caption throughout: 'for example: illustrative scores, not from a real model'; the only other text is the formula p = softmax(z / T).

shots.setting: The case board, 2019–2020, night: a sheet of log-log paper that becomes a night city; then the candle shelf and the Wall of Forecasts
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: AlexNet's waiting slip glints as a straight line is ruled on log-log paper and becomes a night city's skyline; a match cut lights the new candle SCALE IS THE MAIN LEVER. CAMERA: BOARD (the log-log sheet pinned in the lamp's pool), the skyline, then SHELF (low macro; the scale candle lit), then WALL (a slow truck to W4). BOARD MAP (canonical, from the staging appendix; repeated word for word): the Case Board is a fixed grid of slots laid out as network columns by era, left to right: C1 (1943–1969) the far-left input column, C2 (1969–1997), C3 (2006–2017), C4 (2018–2023), and the output, the glowing chat box, at the far right; the case card WHO TAUGHT IT? hangs in slot K at the board's centre; the suspect cards S1 RULES, S2 KNOWLEDGE and S3 LEARNING hang in the left margin, top to bottom; the founding row F1–F2 runs beneath columns C3 and C4; the question-card thread runs along the board's top edge (slots Q1 to Q4, left to right), a low-chroma oxblood string (emberRed rim mixed about 60% into candleAmber) that glints only where the lamp's pool falls; the Wall of Forecasts hangs to the board's right, its slots W1 to W8 left to right (W1 Turing, W2 chess, W3 Rosenblatt 1961, W4 Florence 2012, W5 Coulom, W6 the 30-to-50-years slip in shadow, W7 Hinton 2017, W8 an empty pin until ch15). This chapter works in column C4, the last column before the output (the chat box): ch10's thread-of-light card sits at the foot of column C3, and C4's head slot C4-a waits for this chapter's type sort. STUDY LOCK: the shot opens at the board in candleAmber (the mood field names the opening location). During the lead-in, a sheet of log-log paper is pinned to the board in a sliver of lamp light; on 'law' the fountain pen rules a single straight descending line across it: error falling as a power law as size rises, the axis ticks spanning more than seven powers of ten; both axes carry the small printed lettering 'log scale' (the line is straight only on log-log paper). ONE CITY BEAT, kept short: on 'bigger' the paper tilts back and the ruled line becomes the rising roofline of a single night skyline, the tint crossfading (crossfadeMood, 1.2 s, no dip) from candleAmber to serverCyan as the paper leaves the board, each window a bank of parameters, its tallest tower ninety-six storeys, one per layer of 2020's giant (no districts, no aisles, no location, no chip count). On 'giant' (GPT-3, named aloud) every window lights at once, and a small brass plate at the tower's foot, prop lettering, reads 175 BILLION WEIGHTS (the size is on the prop; the narration no longer says it). On 'examples', in one lit window near the roofline, three worked example strips of cut paper hang (a word and its answer, twice over, then a third pair), and a fourth strip fills itself in on its own; nothing in the tower is re-cut, no pen touches it (few-shot: new tasks from examples in the prompt, without retraining). On 'candle' a straight match-cut from the tallest tower's lit roofline to a candle flame on the shelf, where the tint crossfades back to candleAmber (crossfadeMood, 1 s, no dip; STUDY LOCK), so the shelf and the Wall are lamp-lit: the hero candle SCALE IS THE MAIN LEVER is lit (rising fourth), its base tag reading 2020, no sleeve yet, the flame on the top ring; it is still burning, and still contested, as of October 2026. CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. On 'waiting', while the camera is still on the log-log paper, the pin of the W4 slip at the board's right edge glints once in the lamp's pool (the narrator is retrieving it aloud). After the line, in music only, the camera begins its pan right to the Wall of Forecasts, and as it arrives the slip in W4, pinned in chapter 8 ('…simply by waiting for faster GPUs and bigger datasets…'), catches the light fully and its pin glints again; W6's corner stays half-lit in shadow; W7 holds Hinton's 2017 slip at the far end.

chapters.title: The Last Accomplice, and the Return to the Scene
chapters.blurb: 2017–2023. The last accomplice is a person, choosing: a simulated robot learns from a person's choices between two tries, and people's rankings train a judge that shapes a small model until it is preferred to one a hundred times larger. Then the return to the dark room: not a new engine, a new door, and the first note in the file, written that same day, still holds. The X-ray is complete and Rosenblatt's 1961 note is read over the glowing box: language was the door. A step back to 2021: the first figure through that door is a new lab, founded and told in the same grammar as every lab's founding, money and all (FTX, then Amazon and Google on the ledger). Then a stampede through the door, in the order it happened, ending with OpenAI's GPT-4 and Anthropic's Claude launched the same day; and on the Wall, one slip still half in shadow.

shots.setting: A simulation stage, June 2017, night: a one-legged robot on a checkerboard floor under a lamp; a small desk with two lit screens
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the last accomplice: X-ray band 7's shears-shaped slot glints, and on a simulation stage a hand taps the better of two tries while a one-legged paper robot learns from the taps. CHAPTER INDEX TAB (the film's chapter-card device for clue chapters): at the shot's first frame a manila index tab, typed in Special Elite with the chapter title 'The Last Accomplice, and the Return to the Scene', drops down from the frame's top edge at top-left, like a file-divider tab on a manila folder, holds for 2.5 seconds over the picture, and slides back up (top-left, so it never shares the bottom-left corner with the date stamp); no new shot, no lamp change. The tab rides over the lead-in and the first words of the line. CAMERA: X-RAY, then the stage. A plain cut from ch11-s08's board along the same amber study (study to study; the slot's ink bleed below is the chapter's one signature transition). Open in the study on the X-ray chat box (candleAmber room; the box a serverCyan practical), square-on: its top band, band 7, drawn as a dark, empty, shears-shaped slot. At 0.6 s the slot glints once (a single cold edge-light along the shears' outline), so the eye finds it; then, from 1.0 s to 2.2 s, ink bleeds from that slot (inkBleed origin = the slot) into duskRose, the bleed complete just before the first words of the line. On a paper stage, the Hopper: a one-legged robot cut from black card (thigh, shin, foot) on a checkerboard simulator floor, hopping and toppling. In the foreground, a small desk with two little lit screens side by side, each replaying a short clip of the robot's latest tries. shots.setting: A paper-cut garden at dusk, 2022: a long overgrown hedge, a small neat topiary and a pair of shears; a labeller's desk with two scrolls
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: a paper garden: a person ranks two scrolls, a balance-scale judge tips, the shears snip a vast hedge into a small topiary, and the judges' ribbons go to the small one. A labeller (generic, at a laptop) compares two scrolls of text side by side, their lines soft and illegible, captioned 'machine-generated text', and ranks one above the other. Three garden tools hang in a row on a parchment plate as the three steps of the method: a gardener's sketch (people write example answers), a pair of balance scales, the judge (a reward model learned from their rankings), and the shears, which then move on their own (reinforcement learning against that judge). On 'judge' the scales tip toward the ranked scroll; on 'shaped' the shears lift off the plate by themselves and snip the garden behind, one snip per ranking. On the left, a vast shaggy hedge, untrimmed, with a small paper tag 175B. On the right, a small topiary, shaped by thousands of snips, tagged 1.3B. On 'preferred', a row of anonymous judges each pins a small ribbon on the topiary. As the ribbons are pinned, held through the music-only hold so it can be read, a plain caption at the foot of the plate gives the paper's own caveat: the labellers agreed with each other about 73 times in 100. Text is limited to two items (the result, then the caveat); the three-step plate is told by its pictures and by the narration.

shots.setting: The study, 2022, night: the X-ray chat box fully lit beside the case board; two cards from the file held over it
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: all seven X-ray bands light at last; Rosenblatt's 1961 language slip floats into the box's light, and the shears clue card is pinned. CAMERA: X-RAY, then THE FULL WIDE (one of the three reserved wides). STUDY LOCK: a crossfade, with crossfadeMood serverCyan→candleAmber under it (no dip, no tint pop), from the lit city at the end of the return to the dark room (ch12-s06) into the study, onto the X-ray box; the room is candleAmber under the green-shaded lamp; the era's colour enters only as a practical, the X-ray box glowing serverCyan, its light falling cold across the board and the hands, and the window showing the night sky. The chat box stands translucent as an X-ray plate, framed square-on, with the right-hand edge of column C4 of the case board just in frame at the left, and the fixed internal layout used in every X-ray beat of the film: a single column of seven faint, empty, unlabelled bands, read bottom to top. One slow, even tilt from its base to its top, wordless under music for the whole lead-in, lights every band in order at an even pace, each with one soft scored chime: threshold lanterns, the knobs, hidden layers and a backward arrow, furnaces and a sea of text, attention threads, next-word type sorts, and last, at the top, a pair of preference shears that clicks into the dark slot seen at the start of chapter 12 and lights. The bands carry no words and no dates: each band's era is signalled only by its own object and its chime. The seam between bands 3 and 4 stays dark: pointedly absent are the stencils, the Mark I patch cords and the clean bowl. As the tilt nears the top, Rosenblatt's 1961 slip lifts off its pin at W3 on the Wall of Forecasts and floats into the box's light, arriving as the shears click in, its Special Elite typewriter letters laid over the glowing type sorts, readable through the line and the pause after it (the same fragment as ch03-s08's card). It is read as what it was, a note on what a brain model must one day explain, not a forecast come true: no tick, no glint, no verdict (unlike Coulom's slip). The W3 slip carries, wherever it hangs (here and in ch03-s08), a small typed tag tied to its pin, prop lettering in Special Elite: 'a hunch, not a forecast · 1961', so its place on the Wall of Forecasts does not cast it as a prophecy. On 'door', the hands reach in at frame left and pin this chapter's clue card into slot C4-b, beneath the type sort in C4-a: a pair of garden shears. A breath later the Rosenblatt slip drifts back to its pin and the camera pulls back from the plate to THE FULL WIDE: the case board, the candle shelf and the Wall of Forecasts in one frame, the X-ray box glowing at the board's output, every band lit. Hold the wide, still, for at least the last 2.5 seconds of the shot.
